title: Notes app: decisions before 1.0
subtitle: Open questions from the code review.

project.summary: Two decisions and one test stand between us and the 1.0 release.

items.title: How long do login tokens live?
items.why: Tokens never expire today, so a stolen phone keeps access forever.

details.context: The server issues a token at login and accepts it until the user logs out. There is no refresh step and no server-side list of active tokens.
details.decision: Pick a lifetime. Short tokens need a silent refresh in the app; long ones only need a re-login screen.
details.why: 1.0 freezes the API. Adding expiry later forces every old client to log in again at once.
details.recommendation: 30 days with silent refresh keeps people logged in on a phone they use, and a lost phone loses access within a month. It costs one endpoint and a retry in the app.

options.label: 30 days, refreshed silently while the app is used

items.title: Export format
items.why: People asked for an export, and we have to pick one format to support first.

details.context: Notes are stored as Markdown with a small front matter block. Attachments sit next to them.
details.decision: Which format the Export button writes.
details.why: It is the most requested feature in the beta feedback.
details.recommendation: A zip of Markdown files is what we store anyway. It opens everywhere and needs no converter.

options.label: One JSON file
cons: Nobody can read it by hand

items.title: What should the public beta be called?
items.why: The store listing needs a name by the end of the month.

items.title: Run tests in CI on every push

testing.title: Sync between two phones
steps: Install the beta on two phones.
Edit the same note on both while one is offline.
testing.expect: Both edits survive, the later one on top.

done.title: Tests run on every push
done.detail: CI runs the whole suite in about four minutes.

evidence.title: Method
items: Read the sync and auth modules, ran the test suite, tried login on two devices.
